variants.headline: Looking back: money in hand, no food to buy
variants.sub: People have money for food but cannot buy it because shops and farms are sold out.
variants.body:
We return to our earlier coverage. Our report recorded this: Shops and farms were sold out of food, leaving people with money unable to buy meals.

Money in hand. Nothing to buy for the meal. It is a simple picture of a shortage, and a sharp reminder that a full purse is not a full shelf. Readers should insist that the problem is described plainly before somebody offers an answer to a different kind of hunger.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

The stewardship of {target} requires attention to actual availability. This paper distinguishes the shortage of food from a shortage of money and judges proposed answers against the practical need they must address.
